title: Browser Privacy Security Checklist - Complete Setup Guide
metaDescription: Essential browser privacy and security checklist. Step-by-step guide to configure Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Brave for maximum privacy protection.
intro: Your browser is your gateway to the internet, but it can also be a privacy risk. This comprehensive checklist will help you secure any browser - Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Brave, or privacy-focused options like Incognito Browser - with essential settings and best practices.

items.why: Blocks trackers, ads, and fingerprinting scripts that follow you across websites and collect your browsing data.
items.howTo: Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Enhanced Tracking Protection (Strict). Chrome: Settings > Privacy and Security > Cookies > Block third-party cookies. Safari: Preferences > Privacy > Prevent cross-site tracking.

items.why: Encrypts DNS queries to prevent ISPs and networks from seeing which websites you visit.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and Security > Security > Use secure DNS (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1). Firefox: Settings > Network Settings > Enable DNS over HTTPS. Consider using Quad9 (9.9.9.9) for additional malware protection.

items.why: Prevents websites from accessing your physical location without explicit permission.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and Security > Site Settings > Location > Don't allow sites to see your location. Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Permissions > Location > Block new requests.

items.why: Protects against unauthorized access to your camera and microphone by malicious websites.
items.howTo: Go to browser privacy settings and set Camera and Microphone to 'Ask before accessing' or 'Block'. Review and revoke permissions for sites that don't need them.

items.why: Prevents advertisers and trackers from building profiles across multiple websites you visit.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and Security > Cookies > Block third-party cookies. Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Cookies > Delete cookies when Firefox closes. Enable 'Cross-site tracking cookies'.

items.task: Set browser to clear data on exit
items.why: Automatically removes browsing history, cookies, and cached data when you close the browser.
items.howTo: Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > History > Clear history when Firefox closes. Chrome: Use Incognito mode or extensions like 'Click&Clean'. Consider switching to Incognito Browser for automatic data clearing.

items.why: Prevents browsers from storing and auto-filling passwords, addresses, and payment information that could be accessed by malicious sites.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Autofill > Turn off passwords, payment methods, and addresses. Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Forms and Autofill > Uncheck save options. Use a dedicated password manager instead.

items.task: Change default search engine to privacy-focused option
items.why: Privacy-focused search engines don't track your searches or build advertising profiles.
items.howTo: Set DuckDuckGo, Startpage, or Searx as your default search engine. Chrome: Settings > Search engine. Firefox: Settings > Search. Avoid Google, Bing, and Yahoo for better privacy.

items.why: Stops your browser from sending what you type in the address bar to search engines before you hit enter.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and Security > Sync and Google services > Turn off 'Autocomplete searches and URLs'. Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Address Bar > Uncheck suggestion options.

items.task: Configure safe browsing without data sharing
items.why: Protects against malicious sites while minimizing data sent to Google or other companies.
items.howTo: Chrome: Use 'Standard protection' instead of Enhanced (sends less data to Google). Firefox: Keep 'Block dangerous and deceptive content' enabled. Consider browsers like Brave that use local protection lists.

items.why: Prevents websites from identifying you based on your browser configuration, fonts, screen resolution, and other unique characteristics.
items.howTo: Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Enhanced Tracking Protection > Strict (includes fingerprinting). Use Brave browser or Incognito Browser for built-in fingerprinting protection. Chrome users need extensions like uBlock Origin.

items.task: Consider JavaScript restrictions for sensitive browsing
items.why: Many tracking and fingerprinting techniques rely on JavaScript. Selective blocking improves privacy.
items.howTo: Install uBlock Origin and enable medium or hard blocking modes. Firefox users can try NoScript extension. For maximum privacy, use Incognito Browser which includes intelligent script blocking.

items.why: Browser extensions can block additional trackers, ads, and privacy violations that built-in protections miss.
items.howTo: Install uBlock Origin (ad/tracker blocking), ClearURLs (removes tracking parameters), and Decentraleyes (blocks CDN tracking). Avoid too many extensions as they can create unique fingerprints.
